title: CB-PFR full-paper computational run summary

source.locations: Tables 6, 13, 15–18 and Sections IV.2.4–IV.3.6, PDF pp. 8–18
source.limitation: This browser-ready file contains aggregate values transcribed from the paper draft, not raw statepoint/HDF5 outputs. Use archived run artefacts as the primary record when available.

campaign.name: C5G7 transport campaign — OpenMC and deterministic S_N
campaign.historiesInterpretation: Exact sum of the five phase totals is 4,090,540,000 configured active histories; Table 6 rounds this to 4.0905 × 10^9. This is not the number of independent design observations.

phases.role: Six-layout screening; three seeds per layout
Held-out evaluation; three new seeds per layout

canonicalReference.verdict: Internal consistency check passed; not official OECD/NEA benchmark acceptance.

scalingCheck.interpretation: Directionally consistent with H^-1/2 under this campaign, but not a formal verification; only six layouts and P4/P5 may include source-convergence bias.

crossCode.interpretation: The two codes give the same k-effective ordering across four paper-inferred classes, but peak metrics reorder classes. Spatial differences are too large to call this physical validation.

selectionComparison.independentUnits: Three held-out seeds per layout; 10,000 bootstrap resamples are not 10,000 independent OpenMC experiments.
selectionComparison.conclusion: This transport campaign does not demonstrate CB-PFR superiority over point estimate or uniform margin.

findings.title: Budget changes the screening decision
findings.body: The lowest-budget P1 selected MUUM (F_fission proxy 1.3078). The P5 held-out mean was lowest for MMUU (1.296065), with MUMU close behind (1.296538). The paper reports P1-selection regret 0.0203, about 1.6%, against the P5 empirical reference; that reference is not exact physical truth.

findings.title: Canonical k-effective consistency check
findings.body: For canonical UMMU, OpenMC reported k_eff = 1.186470 versus the cited 1.18655 reference: −8.0 pcm, z = 0.84. This passes the paper's internal threshold only; it is not official benchmark acceptance.

findings.title: Cross-code ranking depends on the metric
findings.body: The k-effective ordering agrees (Kendall τ = 1.00 across four inferred classes), while the peak-power metric gives τ = 0.67. The spatial RMS difference is 7.53–7.91%, so the S_N comparison is not physical validation.

findings.title: No observed selector superiority in this campaign
findings.body: Point estimate, uniform margin and CB-PFR all select MMUU at P4 and P5. Mean held-out regret is 2.32×10⁻⁵ for point estimate and uniform margin versus 3.65×10⁻⁵ for CB-PFR, under the paper's stated empirical reference and three-seed design.

findings.title: Error scaling is consistent, not certified
findings.body: P1-to-P4 RMS deviations change from 339 to 18.5 pcm for k_eff (ratio 18.3, predicted 17.4), and from 0.0242 to 0.0019 for the assembly proxy (ratio 12.7). The paper treats this as a plausibility check, not a precision verification.

limitations: Source/eigenvalue convergence is not certified for this campaign, even though statepoint structure, MGXS presence and uniqueness checks passed.
Only six enumerated layouts and three seeds per layout were used at P4/P5; the evidence does not support broad statistical generalization.
The four symmetry classes are inferred from the deterministic S_N results and the stated position convention; their mapping still needs confirmation against the repository's position map.
The OpenMC assembly-integrated F_fission proxy is not absolute thermal power, pin-power peaking, or a reactor-safety metric.
P5's mean is an empirical held-out reference, not exact ground truth. Bootstrap resamples do not create additional independent simulations.
The six layouts were enumerated; the QUBO-variable-to-material-placement mapping is not implemented in this campaign.

relatedArchivedReplay.note: This is a separate archived observation/replay campaign already represented under the existing Experiments & paper section. Do not merge its rows with the 46-run P1–P5 campaign.
